The post Hakimi favourite to retain the CAF Best Player award appeared first on KBC Digital.

]]> Moroccan and Paris Saint-Germain right-back Achraf Hakimi is tipped to retain his CAF Best Footballer of the Year award following a stellar performance in 2026.

The highest-ranked African player in the 2026 Ballon d’Or standings (13th) overall is the only African player to have established himself among the world’s elite for two consecutive years.

The Atlas Lions captain was crowned Africa’s finest player last year, and he has made great strides this year again after winning back-to-back UEFA Champions League titles for his club PSG, adding to the French Ligue 1 and the UEFA Super Cup.

His individual brilliance propelled Morocco to the final of the 2025 AFCON in their backyard before playing a pivotal role in Morocco’s reaching the quarterfinal of the 2026 FIFA World Cup for a 2nd time in a row.

The best-ranked right-back in the world at the moment has claimed three UEFA Champions League titles (2018, 2025, and 2026), matching Samuel Eto’o’s record as the African player with the most Champions League titles, and has also won seven domestic league titles across Spain, Italy, and France.

Hakimi is the most capped player for his national team with over 100 international caps, including three FIFA World Cup appearances.

Hakimi is among the 26 finalists for the 2026 FIFPRO World 11, following a vote involving 19,806 professional footballers from 73 countries.

He is the  only representative of an African national team among the 26 finalists,in this global selection, Hakimi stands alone in representing African football.

 

Having already been named in the 2025 FIFPRO World 11 and the 2025 FIFA The Best World 11, he has once again been shortlisted for the 2026 FIFPRO World 11.

The winner will be announced on 7th December in Lagos, Nigeria.

The post Hakimi favourite to retain the CAF Best Player award appeared first on KBC Digital.

]]> PPB warns public against misuse of pharmaceutical products https://www.kbc.co.ke/ppb-warns-public-against-misuse-of-pharmaceutical-products/ Thu, 05 Nov 2026 16:44:56 +0000 https://www.kbc.co.ke/?p=158039 The Pharmacy and Poisons Board has cautioned the public against use of pharmaceutical products for the wrong purpose, saying it may cause harm to their health. In an interview with the media on Thursday at the PPB offices in Nairobi, Pharmacy Practices Director Dr. Wilfred Ochieng called on the public to use the medicine based […]

The post PPB warns public against misuse of pharmaceutical products appeared first on KBC Digital.

]]> The Pharmacy and Poisons Board has cautioned the public against use of pharmaceutical products for the wrong purpose, saying it may cause harm to their health.

In an interview with the media on Thursday at the PPB offices in Nairobi, Pharmacy Practices Director Dr. Wilfred Ochieng called on the public to use the medicine based on correct medical advice.

“I would like to advise the public that any medicine should be used based on correct medical advice. Trending or getting viral does not substitute scientific evidence by people who are qualified to provide that kind of evidence”, Dr. Ochieng stated.

He was responding to a social media post which claimed that cetirizine can be used to cause vaginal dryness or achieve vaginal tightening.

The Director clarified that cetirizine is a pharmacy-only medicine, which is classified as an antihistamine.

“This is a medicine that is used to treat allergies. For example, if someone gets allergic rhinitis, also called high fever or you develop some reactions, like itchy skin, or other forms of allergic reactions, then you can take this medicine to relieve such kind of symptoms. That is primarily what cetirizine has been scientifically proven to do”, Dr. Ochieng emphasized.

He also underscored the need to use the right dosage, explaining that medicines are very sensitive items which are put in the market after a rigorous scientific process of product development, discovery and development.

“They are not just any other consumer item and based on that scientific evidence, then the approval will direct you on what it can do and how to get those results. If it says, take orally, it means take it by mouth”, Dr. Ochieng added.

He said PPB has developed a mechanism of ensuring medicines consumed by the public are safe through regulating medicines that are already in the market.

Dr. Ochieng further urged the public to report any form of reaction they may incur as a result of using pharmaceutical products.

“You are encouraged to report anything as long as you have a reason to feel or suspect that the effect is probably due to the medicines you are using”, he reiterated.

 

 

 

The post PPB warns public against misuse of pharmaceutical products appeared first on KBC Digital.

Justice J.N. Abuodha, Thursday issued temporary conservatory orders halting the interviews scheduled for November 12 and 13. The ruling follows a petition (ELRCPET/E005/2026) filed by Thomas Kennedy Balala against IEBC Chairperson Erastus […]

The post Malindi court halts IEBC CEO recruitment, suspends interviews for nine candidates appeared first on KBC Digital.

]]> The Employment and Labour Relations Court in Malindi has suspended the recruitment of the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) Secretary/Chief Executive Officer.

Justice J.N. Abuodha, Thursday issued temporary conservatory orders halting the interviews scheduled for November 12 and 13.

The ruling follows a petition (ELRCPET/E005/2026) filed by Thomas Kennedy Balala against IEBC Chairperson Erastus Edung Ethekon, the Commission and 11 others.

The judge who certified the petition as urgent said the orders will remain in force pending the inter partes hearing scheduled for 17 November 2026.

The candidates seeking to fill the position are Anthony Omerikwa, Halakhe Waqo, Harley Mutisya, Edmund Odiwuor Malitt and Andrew Gitau Kimani.

Others include Mohamed Abdullahi Abdi, Edward Katama Ngeywa, Martina Wato Yattani and Nelly Ilongo.

The Malindi ruling comes amid a separate constitutional petition filed at the High Court in Nairobi by Dr. Augustus Kyalo Muli on Wednesday 4th November, 2026.

Justice R.E. Aburili declined to certify the matter as extremely urgent for ex-parte consideration and directed that it be mentioned on November 11, 2026.

Dr. Muli’s petition challenged the IEBC’s decision to engage KPMG Advisory Services Limited to undertake what the Commission described in its statement of 30 October 2026 as ‘end-to-end recruitment including advertisement, receipt, longlisting, verification and shortlisting.’

The petition raised constitutional questions concerning the independence and mandate of the Commission, particularly under Article 250(12) of the Constitution of Kenya and Section 10 of the IEBC Act.

He questioned whether the delegation of these recruitment functions to an external consultancy is consistent with the constitutional and statutory framework governing appointments to the Commission’s secretariat.

Dr. Muli has also invoked Article 35 of the Constitution, seeking access to critical documents relating to the recruitment, including: The contract between IEBC and KPMG Advisory Services Limited, the recruitment scoring matrix, the resolution of the Commission authorising the engagement and the fees and financial terms of the consultancy arrangement.

Welcoming the development in Malindi, Dr Augustus Kyalo Muli said: “We welcome the Malindi orders. They confirm prima facie urgency. However, since IEBC contests ELRC jurisdiction over Article 250(12) appointments, we will still urge the Constitutional Court in Nairobi on 11 November to grant sustainable protection.”

The post Malindi court halts IEBC CEO recruitment, suspends interviews for nine candidates appeared first on KBC Digital.

]]> Mathare United signs a three-year deal with Blue Triangle Cement https://www.kbc.co.ke/mathare-united-signs-a-three-year-deal-with-blue-triangle-cement/ Thu, 05 Nov 2026 15:35:58 +0000 https://www.kbc.co.ke/?p=158024 Under the partnership, the Blue Triangle Cement logo will be emblazoned on the right sleeve of the club's jersey and on the left side of their playing shorts for all FKF Premier League and FKF Cup fixtures.

The post Mathare United signs a three-year deal with Blue Triangle Cement appeared first on KBC Digital.

]]> Kenyan Premier side Mathare United has signed a three-year partnership with Blue Triangle Cement until 2029.

The agreement was officially unveiled on Thursday and will see Blue Triangle Cement become an official partner of the men’s team currently competing in the Kenyan Premier League until 2029.

Under the partnership, the Blue Triangle Cement logo will be emblazoned on the right sleeve of the club’s jersey and on the left side of their playing shorts for all FKF Premier League and FKF Cup fixtures.

The club’s CEO, Jacton Obure, described the deal as a major step in securing the long-term future of the club.

“This is more than just a sponsorship; it is an investment in the future of Mathare United,” said Mr. Obure. “In a challenging environment for local clubs, securing a partner of the stature and heritage of Blue Triangle Cement gives us the foundation to plan, to grow, and to compete sustainably at the highest level. “We are grateful to Blue Triangle Cement for believing in our vision. When a proudly Kenyan brand chooses Mathare United, it validates our work to professionalize the club and shows that our local game has a future worth believing in,” Obure said.

Blue Triangle Cement’s Head of Commercial and Corporate Affairs, Mr. David Kilonzo, said:

“This is not just another sporting activity, nor is it only about brand visibility. This deal’s core essence is for the nurturing of talent, improving the quality on the pitch so that it can translate to fans in the stadiums.” Kilonzo stated

Mathare, who will be hosting Posta Rangers this weekend, lies 15th in the Kenyan Premier League table on 5 points, having won 1 match, drawn 2, and lost 2 in the 2026/2027 season.

The post Mathare United signs a three-year deal with Blue Triangle Cement appeared first on KBC Digital.

]]> KMTC seeks HELB funding as 20,000 students forfeit training slots over fees https://www.kbc.co.ke/kmtc-seeks-helb-funding-as-20000-students-forfeit-training-slots-over-fees/ Thu, 05 Nov 2026 15:33:23 +0000 https://www.kbc.co.ke/?p=158025 The Kenya Medical Training College (KMTC) has appealed to Members of Parliament to secure Higher Education Loans Board (HELB) financing for its students, warning that exclusion from state financing is forcing thousands of qualified students to abandon their training slots. Appearing before the National Government Constituencies Development Fund (NG-CDF) Committee, chaired by Hon. Musa Sirma, […]

The post KMTC seeks HELB funding as 20,000 students forfeit training slots over fees appeared first on KBC Digital.

]]> The Kenya Medical Training College (KMTC) has appealed to Members of Parliament to secure Higher Education Loans Board (HELB) financing for its students, warning that exclusion from state financing is forcing thousands of qualified students to abandon their training slots.

Appearing before the National Government Constituencies Development Fund (NG-CDF) Committee, chaired by Hon. Musa Sirma, the KMTC management, led by Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Dr. Kelly Oluoch, responded to questions on the status of KMTC projects funded by the NG-CDF Board and a review of constituencies with NG-CDF-funded KMTC campuses.

Dr. Oluoch informed the Committee that although the college trains over 85 per cent of Kenya’s healthcare workforce, its 89,586 students face challenges accessing government financial support because KMTC falls under the Ministry of Health rather than the Ministry of Education.

“KMTC should not have to leave the Ministry of Health to get funded. National financing legislation should recognize KMTC trainees as post-secondary students deserving equitable state funding,” Dr. Oluoch told MPs.

The KMTC CEO said the exclusion is already causing a crisis in admissions and that 20,000 students placed through KUCCPS fail to report every cycle after discovering there is no government scholarship or loan to support them.

Committee members observed that the situation results in a double loss, as students who cannot afford the fees surrender their slots while other qualified applicants miss opportunities because slots have already been allocated.

Hon. Clive Gisairo (Kitutu Masaba) proposed that KMTC and Kenya Universities and Colleges Central Placement Service (KUCCPS) introduce in the meantime, a declaration of ability to pay fees before placement to minimise wastage of admission slots.

“You need a disclaimer during the courses application, informing students that there’s no funding from government for KMTC courses. You should collaborate with KUCCPS for a pop-up message on their portal so that students get the information that those courses are self-sponsored,” said Hon. Gisairo.

However, Hon. Sirma backed KMTC’s plea, questioning why an institution responsible for training the bulk of the country’s healthcare workers should be left out of the Ksh. 300 billion education financing package.

“It makes no sense for KMTC — which trains over 85% of healthcare workers — to be left out simply because it sits under the Ministry of Health rather than the Ministry of Education,” said Hon. Sirma.

Defending KMTC’s placement under the Ministry of Health, Dr. Oluoch argued that training is clinical and depends on hospital attachments, clinical preceptors and health regulatory bodies. He cited Bukura Agricultural College under Agriculture, Kenya Water Institute under Water and Utalii College under Tourism as precedents for specialized colleges staying under line ministries.

To guarantee equitable funding to all students in tertiary institutions across ministries, the KMTC CEO proposed that the envisaged, Tertiary Education Funding Authority (TEFA), sit under the National Treasury.

The post KMTC seeks HELB funding as 20,000 students forfeit training slots over fees appeared first on KBC Digital.

]]> Victims of rights abuses have until 14 November 2026 to file compensation claims https://www.kbc.co.ke/victims-of-rights-abuses-have-until-14-november-2026-to-file-compensation-claims/ Thu, 05 Nov 2026 15:01:04 +0000 https://www.kbc.co.ke/?p=158009 Panel of Experts says it has so far compensated victims to the tune of Ksh1.4 billion, with Phase VII accounting for 157 verified claims worth Ksh96.95 million.

The post Victims of rights abuses have until 14 November 2026 to file compensation claims appeared first on KBC Digital.

]]> Victims of human rights violations, including those injured during demonstrations and public protests, who have not yet filed their claims have until 14 November 2026 to submit their applications to the Panel of Experts on Compensation.

The Panel, chaired by Professor Makau Mutua, urged affected individuals, their families, and beneficiaries to submit their claims before the deadline, cautioning that it would stop receiving new applications after the specified date.

“The Panel continues to receive claims through various official channels and is making progress in processing and compensating claims across different categories of harm. We remain committed to ensuring that no eligible individual is left behind,” stated Professor Mutua.

Prof. Mutua, says the panel has so far made compensation payments amounting to Ksh1.4 billion as it continues to process claims from victims and their beneficiaries.

In an update on Phase VII of the compensation programme, the Panel disclosed that it had processed 157 verified claims, totalling KSh 96.95 million, covering various categories of harm suffered by civilians and uniformed officers.

The claims include cases of fatalities, aggravated injuries, severe injuries, moderate and minor injuries, as well as economic losses stemming from human rights violations, including those committed during demonstrations and public protests.

According to the breakdown, the Panel confirmed it verified and paid one fatality claim valued at Ksh 3 million. Claims under the severe injury category accounted for Ksh 47 million from 47 verified cases.

Moderate injuries accounted for 74 claims valued at Ksh 37 million, while 19 minor injury claims attracted payment of Ksh 950,000. The Panel also processed 11 economic loss claims worth Ksh 550,000.

Aggravated injuries also attracted compensation, with verified claims attracting payments of between KSh 1.5 million and KSh 2.5 million, depending on the category of harm.

Professor Mutua stated that the Panel would observe strict verification and authentication procedures to establish the eligibility of applicants.

“Every claim received shall undergo strict verification and authentication before a decision is reached, and notification to each claimant of the outcome shall be provided within a reasonable time,” he said.

He added that the Panel was engaging victims, their families, and beneficiaries directly to address concerns, clarify the status of applications, and provide updates on the compensation process.

The post Victims of rights abuses have until 14 November 2026 to file compensation claims appeared first on KBC Digital.

]]> Bayern Munich vs Ajax match in Nairobi tickets to cost from Ksh 2,500 says CS Mvurya https://www.kbc.co.ke/bayern-munich-vs-ajax-match-in-nairobi-tickets-to-cost-from-ksh-2500-says-cs-mvurya/ Thu, 05 Nov 2026 14:30:30 +0000 https://www.kbc.co.ke/?p=157993 According to the CS, tickets will only be sold online in phases via www.TalantaSportsCity.com, starting from as low as Ksh 2,500.

The post Bayern Munich vs Ajax match in Nairobi tickets to cost from Ksh 2,500 says CS Mvurya appeared first on KBC Digital.

]]> Tickets for the thrilling match between European giants Bayern Munich from Germany, and Ajax Amsterdam from the Netherlands will be sold from Ksh 2,500 starting Thursday 6 PM EAT.

The eagerly awaited game, scheduled for January 5th, will take place at the 60,000 seater Raila Odinga International Stadium,with the friendly match also set to mark the official opening of this iconic venue, which is set to host the 2027 PAMOJA AFCON matches.

While making the announcement on Thursday afternoon, Sports CS Salim Mvurya said that besides the epic football encounter, spectators will also be treated to a 12-hour fan festival, world-class entertainment
from leading international artists, and a series of exciting activities designed to celebrate sporting excellence, honour Kenyan sporting heroes, and showcase the very best of Kenya to the world.

“I am pleased to confirm that operational preparations are at an advanced stage to ensure that Kenya not only successfully hosts this historic football encounter but also delivers an extraordinary sporting and entertainment experience of a scale and quality rarely witnessed on the African continent. The experience will feature dedicated concierge services, a spectacular 12-hour fan festival, world-class entertainment featuring leading international artists, and a series of exciting activities designed to celebrate sporting excellence, honor our sporting heroes, and showcase the very best of Kenya to the world,” stated Mvurya.

According to the CS, tickets will only be sold online in phases via www.TalantaSportsCity.com, starting from as low as Ksh 2,500.

Other ticket prices includes Ksh 3,500,Ksh 5,000 and Ksh 20,000.

“The tickets will be released in phases across multiple seating categories, with prices starting from as low as Kshs 2,500, reflecting our commitment to making this exceptional sporting experience
accessible to as many Kenyans as possible. Supporters are encouraged to secure their tickets within the announced sales windows, as availability in sold-out categories cannot be guaranteed in subsequent phases. We further urge all supporters to purchase tickets exclusively through official channels and make payments only to verified accounts to avoid fraudulent transactions,” added the CS

 

CS Mvurya made it clear that the match’s funding comes entirely from private sector contributions, easing worries about the use of public funds for the event. He emphasized the government’s promise to deliver a top-tier and memorable AFCON next year, jointly with Tanzania and Uganda.

“Both FC Bayern Munich and AFC Ajax Amsterdam have made firm commitments, in writing, to field their best possible starting elevens for this historic encounter. We are therefore
preparing to welcome two of Europe’s most celebrated football clubs, bringing their elite football talent to Kenyan soil for an exceptional international sporting spectacle,” he concluded.

While Ajax has secured the UEFA Champions League trophy four times, Munich boasts a total of six victories in the competition.

The game will serve as a chance to evaluate the stadium’s functioning, security measures, transportation networks, hospitality offerings, crowd control, and other essential aspects.

The post Bayern Munich vs Ajax match in Nairobi tickets to cost from Ksh 2,500 says CS Mvurya appeared first on KBC Digital.

The authority attributes the increase to enhanced revenue mobilization which has helped it achieve the milestone a month earlier than in previous financial years. In the month of October alone, KRA says it […]

The post Revenue collection hits Ksh 1T in four months to October appeared first on KBC Digital.

]]> Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA) has collected a record Ksh 1.01 trillion on four months of the current fiscal year ending October 2026.

The authority attributes the increase to enhanced revenue mobilization which has helped it achieve the milestone a month earlier than in previous financial years.

In the month of October alone, KRA says it surpassed the revenue collection target by Ksh 2.3 billion after revenue grew to Ksh 260.6 billion against a target of Ksh 258.3 billion, representing a collection rate of 100.9%.

“The October performance reflects a revenue growth of 15.5%, compared to growth rates of 8% and 6.5% recorded in October 2025 and October 2024, respectively. The good performance is attributed to stellar performance by both Customs and Domestic Revenue,” said the authority in a statement.

Customs revenue posted a performance rate of 101.1% after collection grew by 11.3% to Ksh 94.8 billion in October driven by non-oil taxes which recorded a surplus of Ksh 7.2 billion and a growth of 26%.

On the other hand, domestic revenue increased by 18.1% to Ksh 165.4 billion against a target of Ksh 164.1 billion

“The strong performance was driven by above-target collections across several key tax heads, including Domestic VAT, Domestic Excise, Corporation Tax, Individual Income Tax, Capital Gains Tax (CGT) and Stamp Duty,” KRA noted.

KRA says in the month under review, corporation tax realized a collection gain of 31.6% amounting to Ksh 23.9 billion supported by electricity, manufacturing, transportation and wholesale sectors which accounted for approximately 81% of Corporation Tax collections.

“These sectors registered an average installment tax growth of 38.1% during the month, compared to a cumulative growth of 35.9% for the July–October 2026 period.”

Domestic VAT surpassed also surpassed it collection target by Ksh 45 million as collection grew by 22.1% to Ksh 33.4 billion against a target of Ksh 33.3 billion while excise duty surpassed its target for the first time in a long period after posting a surplus of Ksh 945 million and growth of 54.1%.

KRA attribute the ruse in excise duty collection to increased remittances from manufacturers of keg beer, premium beer, wine and spirits, and tobacco that grew 0.3%, 43.5%, 110.8% and 94.1% respectively.

KRA targets to collect Ksh 3.268 trillion by the end of Financial Year 2026/2027.

The post Revenue collection hits Ksh 1T in four months to October appeared first on KBC Digital.

]]> Ruto urges universities to align courses with industry demands https://www.kbc.co.ke/ruto-urges-universities-to-align-courses-with-industry-demands/ Thu, 05 Nov 2026 13:18:27 +0000 https://www.kbc.co.ke/?p=157994 President William Ruto has challenged Kenyan universities to produce graduates capable of addressing society’s most pressing challenges while adapting to a dynamic workplace. The President said universities and technical training institutions must align their academic programmes with the realities of society and the evolving demands of industry. The ultimate measure of education, he said, should […]

The post Ruto urges universities to align courses with industry demands appeared first on KBC Digital.

]]> President William Ruto has challenged Kenyan universities to produce graduates capable of addressing society’s most pressing challenges while adapting to a dynamic workplace.

The President said universities and technical training institutions must align their academic programmes with the realities of society and the evolving demands of industry.

The ultimate measure of education, he said, should not be the certificates graduates acquire but their ability to apply knowledge, create opportunities and contribute meaningfully to national development.

President Ruto made the remarks at State House Nairobi on Thursday during the award of charter to International Leadership University (ILU).

“This is the difference between education that produces qualifications and education that builds capability. Knowledge and expertise matter, but their value lies in their application,” the President said.

He added: “A degree should certify more than what a graduate knows. It should demonstrate what that graduate can achieve.”

Kenya, he stated, needs scientists who develop solutions to diseases, farmers who transform agricultural produce into thriving enterprises, engineers who build for future generations and entrepreneurs who create employment.

At the same time, President Ruto pointed out that the changing nature of work, driven by artificial intelligence, automation and digital technologies, makes it urgent for educational institutions to prepare students for a rapidly evolving global economy.

Citing the World Economic Forum’s “Future of Jobs Report 2025”, he noted that 39 per cent of workers’ skills are expected to change or become outdated by 2030.

The President said Kenya must therefore move away from an education system that emphasises rote learning and examinations at the expense of critical thinking, creativity, practical competence and innovation.

“We cannot build a 21st Century economy with an education system that prepares young people to reproduce yesterday’s answers,” he said.

Kenya’s ambition, President Ruto noted, is to build a knowledge-driven, globally competitive economy supported by a modern services sector capable of exporting technology, financial services, professional expertise and innovation alongside traditional agricultural and manufactured products.

He noted that technology has made it possible for professionals based in Kenya to compete internationally, citing opportunities for software engineers, financial analysts, medical specialists, researchers and creative professionals to serve clients and institutions across the world.

However, he cautioned that such opportunities could only be realised if universities equipped graduates with relevant digital skills, including the ability to use computers, access the Internet, analyse data and apply artificial intelligence.

A major priority, the President explained, must be strengthening the connection between universities and industry through practical training, internships and structured partnerships.

He disclosed that the Government is working towards expanding the National Internship Programme to accommodate 50,000 young college and university students from January 2027.

Incentives, including netting off the stipends they pay from their taxes, will also be introduced to encourage private-sector employers to offer internship opportunities.

The President urged universities to proactively identify internship placements for their students, noting that practical exposure is essential in bridging the gap between academic knowledge and workplace competence.

Within 24 hours of Government advertising the 50,000 paid internship opportunities, 150,000 young people have already applied, the President announced.

Additionally, Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises State Department has advertised for a training programme for 600,000 young people – and progressively up to one million – to enable them access business opportunities in the Access to Government Procurement Opportunities. Already, 200,000 applications have been received within 24 hours.

He encouraged young people to register and take advantage of the opportunities, adding that the Government will facilitate free business registration and access to financing.

Meanwhile, the President underscored the importance of equity in education and economic opportunity, stating that fairness must be reflected in Government policy and resource allocation.

“When I said ‘Bottom Up’, it was not a slogan. Now I am saying, ‘Usawa ni Sawa’, it is not a slogan. I mean it. Equity must inform Government policy,” he said.

He cited investments in education as evidence of his commitment to expanding opportunities, noting that in the 2026/27 financial year, the education sector has been allocated KSh784.5 billion, up from KSh527 billion in 2022/23, representing an increase of 49 per cent.

The President also cited the introduction of a student-centred university funding model through which scholarships and loans are allocated according to students’ financial needs.

President Ruto also used the occasion to underscore the importance of leadership grounded in service and measurable results, and not titles or positions.

He cited the example of Mr Peter Tabichi, a mathematics and physics teacher at Keriko Mixed Day Secondary School in Nakuru County, who was named the world’s best teacher in 2019.

The President said despite teaching in a school with only one computer, poor Internet connectivity and a teacher-to-student ratio of 1:58, Mr Tabichi demonstrated exceptional initiative.

“He downloaded learning materials from Internet cafés for offline use and donated 80 per cent of his monthly income to support his students,” he said.

His students, the President added, subsequently won a Royal Society of Chemistry Award for a project that generated electricity from local plants.

When asked what his philosophy was, Mr Tabichi gave a simple answer: “You have to do more and talk less.”

The President said this is the kind of leadership Kenya needs and the values universities should deliberately cultivate.

He challenged ILU to distinguish itself through the quality of leaders it nurtures and the practical impact of its graduates.

Education Cabinet Secretary Migos Ogambo called on universities to measure their success by the quality of teaching, the value of research and their contribution to solving challenges facing Kenya and the wider world.

ILU Chancellor Kivutha Kibwana commended the Government for guiding the institution on the journey towards becoming a fully fledged university.

Prof Kibwana also called for leadership training to be integrated into the curriculum at all levels of education.

The ceremony was also attended by ILU Board of Trustees Chairman Daniel Musinga, Vice-Chancellor Timothy Kiruhi and Commission for University Education Chairman James Onyango Awino, among other dignitaries.

]]> Progress against malaria: Kenya reports 34% decline in cases https://www.kbc.co.ke/progress-against-malaria-kenya-reports-34-decline-in-cases/ Thu, 05 Nov 2026 12:33:17 +0000 https://www.kbc.co.ke/?p=157982 Health CS Aden Duale credits stronger disease control efforts but urges action to close an 85 per cent funding gap.

The post Progress against malaria: Kenya reports 34% decline in cases appeared first on KBC Digital.

]]> Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale has disclosed that the country has recorded a 34 per cent decline in confirmed malaria cases.

Duale said the progress reflects targeted efforts by the Government of Kenya, which is intensifying its drive to eliminate malaria, through greater domestic investment, stronger community health services, improved disease surveillance, and local production of essential health commodities.

According to figures cited by the Health CS, Kenya recorded a significant drop in confirmed malaria cases, from 5.54 million in 2023 to 3.64 million in the year to September 2026.

“Incidence among children under five also decreased from 194 to 119 cases per 1,000,” he added, indicating progress in protecting one of the most vulnerable populations.

However, Duale, who represented President William Ruto at the High-Level Dialogue on Malaria Elimination in Gaborone, Botswana, stressed that sustaining these gains requires adequate and predictable financing. He highlighted Kenya’s substantial shortfall in resources needed to implement its malaria strategy.

“Kenya needs KSh17.7 billion annually to implement its malaria strategy, against the KSh2.66 billion available this year, leaving an 85% funding gap,” he stated.

The funding deficit arises amid increasing pressure on African governments to bolster domestic health financing as international development assistance becomes less predictable.

To address this challenge, Duale noted that Kenya is integrating malaria interventions into its Universal Health Coverage reforms, with investments directed towards community health services, primary healthcare, and digital surveillance systems.

He also said the government is implementing measures to combat antimalarial drug resistance through multiple first-line therapies and enhanced pharmacovigilance, which aims to monitor the safety and effectiveness of malaria medicines.

A key pillar of the government’s strategy is strengthening Kenya’s pharmaceutical and health products manufacturing capacity. This initiative seeks to reduce reliance on imported commodities and improve access to essential supplies.

“Through the Health Products and Technologies Local Manufacturing Strategy, Kenya is targeting local production of 50% of essential health commodities,” he said.

“Our growing capacity to manufacture spatial repellents, with trials showing a reduction in malaria infections of about 33%, demonstrates the potential of African innovation to advance disease prevention,” the CS explained.

Beyond domestic interventions, Duale called for stronger regional cooperation, particularly in surveillance and coordinated responses to cross-border malaria transmission.

He cited Kenya’s collaboration with Uganda on joint surveillance and emphasised the need for greater coordination through the East African Community, acknowledging that malaria transmission transcends national boundaries.

The CS said African countries must strengthen partnerships and collective action to accelerate progress towards malaria elimination, especially as the continent continues to bear a significant share of the global disease burden.

The post Progress against malaria: Kenya reports 34% decline in cases appeared first on KBC Digital.

]]>
